title: Elementary vector measure question: what am I doing wrong? (MathOverflow question 25141)
authors: G. Rodrigues (question); answers by Bill Johnson and fedja
exact_version: Asked 2010-05-18; page read 2026-10-21 (full text incl. both answers)
section_locator: Question body: EXAMPLE paragraph (indicator map chi: Omega -> L^infinity(Omega), finitely additive, bounded, unbounded variation); paragraph citing 'proposition 11, pg. 4 of the Diestel-Uhl monograph' for the fundamental inequality; sentence 'if the codomain B is finite-dimensional then the variation and the semivariation agree (note: this fails in every infinite-dimensional space by Dvoretzky-Rogers)'.
relevance: Direct prior art for the example class: an indicator-valued vector measure with bounded range/semivariation and infinite variation. States the finite-dimensional equivalence and its infinite-dimensional failure.
limits: Community source, peer-reviewed only by site voting. The stated example is the L^infinity (finitely additive) version; the countably additive L^q version for q < infinity is not stated there. Community discussion is not a primary theorem source or a substitute for the explicit analytic proofs in the report; no technical conclusion is accepted on voting evidence.
assumptions: finitely additive Banach-valued measures on Boolean algebras; semivariation in the dual form sup over ||b*||<=1 of |b*u|(E)
conclusion: Community discussion of bounded-semivariation versus bounded-variation and indicator examples. Finite-dimensional boundedness classes coincide, but numerical variation and semivariation need not be equal.
proof_status: Discussion-level; the question's own 'proof' was refuted in the answers (Lemma 2 false); the example and finite-dim statement were not challenged

title: On functions of bounded semivariation
exact_version: arXiv:1501.05196, read via ar5iv full-text HTML rendering (https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1501.05196) on 2026-10-21; also published in Real Anal. Exchange 40(2) (2015) per Project Euclid listing (published version not accessed)
section_locator: Definition 1.1 (semivariation for operator-valued functions on intervals); Theorem 2.12 (dual characterization SV = sup over ||y*||<=1 of var(y* o F)); Section 3 after Remark 3.2: 'if Y is a finite dimensional Banach space, we have F in SV iff F in BV'; Example 3.3 (ell_2-valued function of bounded semivariation and infinite variation); References [9] Diestel-Uhl record and [12] Dvoretzky-Rogers record
relevance: Accessible full-text anchor for: (a) the semivariation concept and dual characterization; (b) the finite-dimensional equivalence of bounded variation and bounded semivariation; (c) an infinite-dimensional example of bounded semivariation with infinite variation; (d) exact bibliographic records for D&U 1977 and Dvoretzky-Rogers 1950.
limits: Treats functions on intervals, not set functions on sigma-algebras; Remark 1.2 notes the measure-theoretic formulation differs slightly and cites D&U and Debieve for it. Survey, not original-theorem source for the finite-dim equivalence. Coordinator version pin uses the primary arXiv submission history (only v1); it does not assert a new coordinator full-text read.
assumptions: Banach-space-valued functions on [a,b]; operator-valued semivariation via bilinear pairing
conclusion: SV <= var always; equality of SV-finiteness and BV-finiteness in finite-dimensional codomain; infinite-dim counterexample
proof_status: Self-contained proofs included in the survey
version: arXiv:1501.05196v1, submitted 21 January 2015; worker read unversioned ar5iv full-text HTML. Coordinator verified on 2026-10-21 that arXiv lists only v1, so the read resolves unambiguously to v1. Published version not read.
